title: How Zach Yadegari built Cal AI to $2M/month at 17: aha-feature apps, influencer ROI, and yearly pricing
summary: Zach lays out his repeatable playbook for viral consumer apps: find one captivating "aha" feature, ship an MVP in a month, test with the single ideal influencer, and scale only when influencer ROI is profitable. He also covers pricing tests, co-founder equity, copycats, and his build-fast, ship-many mindset.

principles.text: Start marketing-first: find one eye-catching 'aha' feature, then build the whole product around it.
principles.quote: I always like to think about things from a marketing first perspective. I like to find an idea that is eye-catching, that is captivating, that is useful, and then build a full product around it.

principles.text: Keep the MVP to the main feature plus the minimum around it, and ship it within a month.
principles.quote: getting an MVP out, which I don't like to spend more than a month on, which should basically be that main feature, and then the minimum amount of components around that to still give a good user experience.

principles.text: Validate with the one ideal influencer in the niche; if it fails with them, rework or scrap the idea.
principles.quote: if that's your ideal influencer for the product and it doesn't work with them, it's not going to work with anyone.

principles.text: Judge influencers by views and predicted ROI, not followers; the hard part is estimating ROI before paying.
principles.quote: Followers don't matter at all. It's only the views they get.

principles.text: Let creators make native content and sneak the product in; don't dictate the creative.
principles.quote: We just want them to plug in our product into the content that already works really well for them and almost sneak it in there.

principles.text: A/B test paywalls and prices; a cheaper yearly plan with a free trial beat a higher price on revenue per download.
principles.quote: because more people would subscribe to the 30 a year, we would make more money on average per download.
